newsitem.title: USA: ITT sells Madison Square Garden stake for $650 million.
newsitem.headline: ITT sells Madison Square Garden stake for $650 million.

text.p: ITT Corp., which is fending off a hostile $6.5 billion takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp., said Thursday it would sell its half interest in New York's famous Madison Square Garden arena to its partner Cablevision Systems Corp. for $650 million.
The deal includes the New York Knicks basketball and Rangers hockey professional sports teams and the MSG television network.
New York-based ITT, whose operations include the Sheraton hotel chain and Caesars casino business, said the deal valued the arena and associated properties at $1.53 billion.
The sale of the arena by ITT was seen as the latest step in the company's defence against Hilton's takeover attempt.
"This agreement to monetize our $360 million investment in MSG is another important step in increasing value for ITT shareholders," ITT Chairman Rand Araskog said in a statement.

ITT last month rejected Hilton's $55-a-share bid and announced a plan to consider the sale of non-core assets and focus on its hotel and casino operations. ITT's other non-core assets include its international telephone directories business.
Despite the sale, Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton said it had no immediate plans to change its bid for ITT.
"Our bid is still our bid," Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman said. "There's no immediate plan to change our bid."
Hilton President Stephen Bollenbach said in a statement the company was pleased that ITT has decided to sell non-core assets such as Madison Square Garden.

"This move by ITT makes the ultimate job of selling non-strategic assets that much easier, enhances our interest in the company and strengthens our resolve to make this combination a reality," Bollenbach said.

Hilton offered to acquire ITT in January for a combination of cash and stock worth $6.5 billion. Hilton also offered to assume $4 billion in debt, bringing the total value of the deal to $10.5 billion.
Cablevision, which teamed up with ITT in 1995 to buy the arena, had been seen as the leading candidate to acquire the Garden stake from ITT.

"Madison Square Garden is as much a New York treasure as Central Park or Times Square," Cablevision Chairman Charles Dolan said in a statement. "Its stewardship carries great responsibility to the city and the fans who have always supported it, and it is great news that the ownership of the Garden remains where it belongs -- in New York."
Sources close to ITT said no formal bids had been received from other parties, although the company held serious conversations with several other companies that had expressed interest.
ITT said the deal would give it an 81 percent gain in a two-year period over its original net investment of $360 million in the arena.
"This has been an extremely successful investment for ITT over the past two year," Araskog said.

Under the deal, Woodbury, N.Y.-based Cablevision, the nation's sixth-largest operator of cable television systems, initially will pay ITT $500 million in cash for a 38.5 percent stake in the properties at the expected closing in June.

ITT also has the option to require Cablevision to purchase the remaining 11.5 percent stake in the arena for $150 million in the two years following the closing of the deal. Should ITT not exercise that option within three years, Cablevision will have the right to acquire the stake from ITT.

Separately, Hilton said a U.S. District Court judge in Nevada declined to grant Hilton's motions seeking to prevent ITT from increasing the size of its board or interfering with the board election process.
In making the decision, the court said it could not rule in Hilton's favour because ITT had not done anything yet to affect the board election process.
ITT said it was pleased with the court ruling.

"It represents the spirit and letter of the law," an ITT spokesman said. "We are satisfied that the merits of our position were upheld in this case, especially since we have not attempted to change our bylaws, nor have we increased the number of our directors."
